label: model_selection_iter5
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Final attempt: keep the bagging family that produced the best ranking so far (extra_trees, best-cut ceiling 0.9434, roc_auc 0.9816) but change the one ranking-axis lever inside it that has never been touched — the split randomisation width. Refit extra_trees with n_estimators raised to 2000 (finer-grained averaged vote ranking, which is what balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut reads) and max_features raised from the implicit 'sqrt' (~7 of 57 columns per split) to 0.35 (~20 columns per split), with min_samples_leaf=1, max_depth=None, class_weight=null, on the same median-imputed, unscaled matrix. Preprocessing and class_weight are held exactly as in iteration 3 so the only difference is the amount of information each randomised split can see. Spambase's signal is spread over a handful of strong columns (word_freq_remove, word_freq_your, word_freq_000, char_freq_$) plus many weak-to-none columns; with max_features='sqrt' most splits in a fully-random forest never see a strong column, which caps the ordering quality that averaging can recover. Widening the candidate set at each split is the one untried way to raise the ranking rather than move the cut. I will read roc_auc, pr_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against iteration 3's 0.9816 / 0.9739 / 0.9434. Cost is safe: iteration 3 took 5.3 s, so 2000 trees at ~3x candidate features is on the order of 30-40 s of the 600 s budget with no memory risk at 2,760 x 57.",
  "model_family": "bagging",
  "candidate_models": [
    "extra_trees"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 2000,
    "min_samples_leaf": 1,
    "max_features": 0.35,
    "class_weight": null,
    "bootstrap": false,
    "n_jobs": -1,
    "random_state": 44
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Iteration 4 was svc<path> on scaled columns; this is not that. Against the best attempt (iteration 3, extra_trees) it is also not a repeat: n_estimators 1000 -> 2000 and max_features left implicit ('sqrt', ~7 of 57 columns per split) -> 0.35 (~20 columns per split), with min_samples_leaf, max_depth, class_weight and the whole preprocessing block held identical. No boosted-tree point, no class_weight move, no threshold-dependent reasoning.",
  "rationale": "cut_headroom on the best attempt is 0.005446 against a 0.0290 shortfall, so 81% of the remaining distance is on the ranking axis and the operating-point lever (class_weight) is exhausted — the Critic's own numbers, and the goal note's ceiling argument, both say so. Capacity control has already been measured as not paying (iteration 2 closed train_val_gap 0.0645 -> 0.0479 with no validation gain), so more regularisation is out. Four families have been fit and no untried family here is a plausible ranking improvement over extra_trees: logreg is the baseline (0.9058), decision_tree and knn are strictly weaker on 57 skewed sub-unit columns, mlp is the only remaining high-capacity option but with 2,760 rows and heavy skew it is a worse bet than the family that already holds the best ranking. That leaves the one lever inside the best family that has never been varied and that acts on the ranking rather than the cut: how many candidate columns each randomised split may consider. With ~7 of 57 candidates most extra-trees splits in this dataset draw only weak<path> columns, which directly degrades the averaged ordering; 0.35 keeps substantial randomisation (so the variance-reduction property that gave 0.9816 roc_auc is preserved) while making it likely every split can reach at least one of the strong spam markers, and doubling the tree count reduces the residual Monte-Carlo noise in the averaged probability so the ranking that is there is actually expressed. I expect a movement of the same order as the family swaps measured here (0.002-0.008 roc_auc), i.e. this will very likely land near 0.938-0.945 balanced_accuracy and not reach 0.967; the honest read is that the 0.967 bar sits 0.0472 of KS above what these 57 columns support with no feature construction available, and this attempt spends the last iteration on the highest-value ranking lever left rather than on a confirmation refit that cannot change the reported best.",
  "unsupported_claims": [],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 5
}
